chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the newborn.

He said: It is named on the seventh day, and an Aqeeqa is performed for it, and its head is shaved, and silver equal to the weight of its hair is given in charity, and the leg is sent to the midwife along with the shoulder, and one feeds from it, and gives in charity.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals for a newborn on the seventh day in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the comprehensive ritual framework for welcoming a newborn, emphasizing gratitude through Aqeeqa and the symbolic purification of shaving the head. It highlights the social dimension of these rites by mandating the distribution of meat to the midwife and the poor, reflecting the Shia emphasis on communal welfare and recognizing the mother's role. The practice of giving silver equal to the hair's weight underscores the value of charity in marking the child's entry into the community.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the new-born, having said: ‘Name it during the seventh day, and perform Aqeeqa for him, and shave off his head, and give silver in charity by the weight of his hair, and send to the mid-wife with the leg (of the sacrificial animal) along with the leaf (silver or gold), and feed from it, and give charity’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from abu Basir who has said the following: “About a newborn abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The child must be given a name on the seventh day, ‘Aqiqah must be offered, his head shaved, silver equal to the weight of his hairs should be given in charity, one leg and hip should be sent to al-Qabilah (the special nurse, doctor), and the rest of the meat should be used for food and as charity.’”
